trigger: The initial strict one-second protocol yielded 0 eligible static sessions and 4 driving sessions with 64 scored seconds. The revision was specified after inspecting coverage counts, before reading per-method field errors. Strict results remain a separate sensitivity check.
source_and_frozen_models: Same archive, 83 sessions, two-second delivery delay, six frozen quantizers/predictors, error target and bootstrap as protocol.json. No model or calibration updates.
clock: Advance a one-second public clock. In an isolated gap of one or two missing seconds, each scheduled feedback report may use only the last measured SNR. Restart when adjacent measured timestamps are more than three seconds apart, time is reversed, or an unparseable timestamp occurs. At duplicate timestamps use the first valid measurement. Reset each session and segment. Hold is used only as an observation available to the feedback encoder.
target: After 40 startup seconds score complete four-second reporting groups containing four actual valid observations. Never impute targets. Discard the incomplete tail. All equal-budget schemes emit exactly four reverse information bits per complete four seconds, whether the schedule called for one or four reports. The raw handset SNR is evaluated without clipping. Counts of held encoder seconds and eligible seconds are reported.
primary: Same paired session-equal RMSE and six methods as the strict protocol; results describe these time-stamped signal logs only. For first-pass transfer use the simulation-fitted predictor; report direct sample-and-hold alongside it.
